text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated capacity saturation detected on pool dedicated-eu1. Error rate/latency SLOs degrading for several tenants. Autoscaler reports placement rejects and slot evictions.

oncall-jordan: seeing 500s and 200-400ms latency spikes across gen endpoints, started ~23:12 UTC.

sre-anjali: evictions spiked at 23:10, placement logs show a surge of small-slot allocations and a bunch of kernel-fallbacks to slow path. attaching quick grep below.

eng-runtime-miguel: can you paste the placement/gpu-allocator logs? suspect kernel selector picked fallback kernels because batch shapes changed.

sre-anjali: ````
2025-06-02T23:09:58Z placement: alloc tenant=acme size=g4dn.xlarge prefer_affinity=false slot_id=null
2025-06-02T23:10:01Z runtime: kernel_selector: selected=fallback_int8 path=slow_kern_v2 reason=quant_mismatch
2025-06-02T23:10:03Z kvcache: miss_rate=0.87 host=hotshard-7 evict_count=412
````

eng-infra-lee: noticed a quota config change in eu1 last night: the per-tenant reserved_slots rollback didn't apply, so packer started bin-packing more tenants into smaller slot sizes. that could change batch distributions.

product-elaine: which tenants are impacted most? any enterprise customers hitting SLA?

sre-anjali: top offenders: acme, zoomly, docsly — all on dedicated-eu1 reserved pools. zoomly alerting on 99th percentile tokens.

eng-runtime-miguel: that quota misconfig could cause multiple small requests to share the same slot which increases variance in sequence lengths => kernel_selector may choose safer (but slower) kernel to handle mixed shapes, and KV cache thrash from many different contexts = throughput drop.

oncall-jordan: any quick mitigation we can push now? rolling restart of packer? temp throttle some tenants?

eng-infra-lee: can rate-limit the noisy tenants from the control plane. quick command: `kubectl exec -n infra packer-ctl -- ./packerctl throttle-tenant --tenant zoomly --qps 20`

eng-runtime-miguel: short-term patch: force kernel_selector to prefer fast_kern_v3 for known model families in eu1 until batch shapes stabilize. I can flip a flag in runtime: `/api/v1/runtime/config/kernel_preference=fast_kern_v3 --env=eu1` but risk tail errors for unusual quant formats.

data-sam: profiling snapshot attached — heavy tail on KV miss latency and lots of small continuous evictions. I think prefix/KV caching boundaries are misaligned when packer bins heterogeneous sessions.

sre-anjali: rolling mitigation plan: 1) throttle top noisy tenants (lee) 2) revert the quota change to previous reserved_slots policy (lee) 3) temporarily bias kernel selector for eu1 to fast path (miguel) 4) disable aggressive packer heuristic for 30m (miguel) 5) monitor evictions/kvmiss and 99p latency (jordan).

eng-infra-lee: reverting quota now, running `terraform apply -target=module.dedicated.eu1.reserved_slots` — ETA ~6m.

eng-runtime-miguel: applying kernel bias now to eu1 runtime fleet (feature-flag flip). pushing and rolling out canary to 5 nodes first.

oncall-jordan: can we also add a temporary routing rule to spill extra requests to hosted pool for the most impacted tenants?

product-elaine: yes — rooftop hosted fallback is acceptable for zoomly for next 1 hour per agreement. please keep me posted so I can notify account.

sre-anjali: after throttling/rollback/kernelflip: eviction rate dropped 78%, kv miss rate down to 0.32 within ~12m, 99p latency drifting back toward SLO.

eng-runtime-miguel: we saw expected improvement on canary nodes; rolling to 100% in eu1 now. leaving kernel selector telemetry verbose for next 2h.

eng-infra-lee: quota rollback completed at 23:28 UTC. packer stable now.

data-sam: posting perf diffs: before mitigation 99p gen latency 2.8s, after mitigations 99p 1.1s. KV eviction count down from 412/min to 86/min. adding to postmortem data.

oncall-jordan: incident state: mitigated. will start postmortem runbook. tagging SE/account teams. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
__notes: generated slack thread for incident-style dedicated capacity saturation investigating kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV cache behavior and quota misconfiguration. matches agents.md schema.
